note: Burmese, Cambodian, Lao and Bruneian dishes — the mainland Southeast Asian repertoires the earlier country rounds did not reach. WEB SEARCH WAS UNAVAILABLE FOR THIS ROUND: every figure is a model estimate reasoned from the dish's own ingredients and anchored against comparable rows the catalogue already holds (the Thai round's noodle bowls and som tam, the Vietnamese round's phở and bánh mì, the Malaysian nasi and mee rows, the MyFCD component rows). Nothing was read off a published table, so every row is verified:false and source:model_estimate. Brunei is deliberately thin: Bruneian and Malaysian cooking are close to the same repertoire and the catalogue already holds Ambuyat, Cacah Binjai, Cacah Tempoyak, Linut, Nasi Katok, Kuih Kelupis, Kuih Pinjaram, Kuih Cincin, Kuih Jala, Kuih Tahi Itik, Wajid Sabah, Pulut Panggang, Bubur Pedas, Air Katira and Sagol, so only what is genuinely Brunei's own is written here and the rest was widened with foods:alias. Where a name collides with a Thai or Vietnamese row already in the catalogue the country leads the name (Lao Larb Moo against Larb Moo, Lao Khao Soi against Khao Soi Gai). Portions are the local street portion: a Burmese mohinga is the standard bowl, a danbauk is one plate, a Lao sticky rice basket is the one that comes with the meal, and a Khmer num pang is one 20 cm baguette. The Cambodian and Lao blocks were added in a second sitting under the same conditions — no web search, every figure a model estimate. Lao dishes that turned out to BE a catalogue row under another name were aliased rather than rewritten: khao niaw onto Khao Niao, sai oua onto Sai Ua, ping gai onto Gai Yang, ping moo onto Moo Ping, khanom kok onto Khanom Krok, khao lam onto Kralan. Lao larb was written only where the preparation genuinely parts from the Thai rows — padaek and dill rather than fish sauce and sugar — and only for pork, duck and fish; chicken and beef were left to Larb Gai and Larb Neua. Lao Khao Soi carries Luang Prabang in its name because it is a clear tomato-pork broth and the catalogue's Khao Soi rows are the northern Thai coconut curry, which is a different dish wearing the same two syllables.
